sections.title: Composition intro
sections.summary: A Flexible Layout screen is one you build yourself: you add sections — text, media, a product catalog, buttons, lists and more — then stack, size and align them however you like. The settings below cover what is unique to assembling the screen; each section type’s own content and styling lives in its own guide (see the note at the end).

sections.title: Link product-aware sections
sections.summary: Some Flexible Layout sections can read the visitor’s current Product Catalog selection. For a paywall, add a Product Catalog section, then link a Text section and a Purchase Button section to that catalog through each section’s “Linked to section” dropdown. The linked Text section can show the selected product description label, and the linked Purchase Button can show the selected product purchase label.

sections.title: Flexible Sections — every setting
sections.summary: The build-your-own screen — you stack sections (text, media, product catalog, buttons, lists…) and arrange them: add / reorder / rename / delete, set each section’s size, fill, alignment, border, padding and margin, control whole-screen scroll and padding, and link product-aware sections (for example Text or Purchase Button) to a Product Catalog so labels and purchases follow the selected product. Each section type’s own content and styling lives in its dedicated block article. This guide documents every setting of the Flexible Sections block, grouped by area. Each setting matches a real control in the screen editor.

sections.title: Flexible Sections section
sections.summary: Builds a FlexibleLayout screen from stacked sections you arrange yourself, giving full control over the vertical order, sizing, and spacing of pieces (media, text, buttons). Use it when the standard screen types do not give you the layout you need.

sections.title: Where it appears
sections.summary: Covered screen types: FlexibleLayout.

sections.title: Add a new section
sections.summary: Use + Add to choose what kind of block to place on this FlexibleLayout screen: text, media, product catalog, button, purchase button, list, custom embed, text field, spacer, header, footer, or paywall header. Add sections in the same order a visitor should read them, then drag to reorder if the screen flow changes. Start with the biggest structure first — for example header, hero text/media, products, and CTA — then tune layout settings inside each section.

sections.title: Background fill color
sections.summary: Sets the color behind this section's content, used when the background type is Solid. The default is white. Enter a hex code or pick a swatch, and keep it in line with your theme so the screen feels on-brand, with enough contrast against the text on top to stay readable.

sections.title: Solid color or image behind
sections.summary: Sets what fills the area behind this section's content. Solid (the default) uses one color you pick below; Media places an image behind the content for a richer, ad-style look. If you go with Media and put text on top, keep the text readable with a darker image or an overlay so your value proposition doesn't get lost.

sections.title: Outline color
sections.summary: Sets the color of the section's outline. The default is black, and it only shows when the border thickness is above 0, so set a width first. Match it to one of your theme's accent colors for a clean, on-brand frame around the section.

sections.title: Outline thickness
sections.summary: Draws an outline around the section. The default 0 means no border; 1 to 2 pixels gives a subtle frame that makes a section read as a self-contained card or highlights an offer. Set this above 0 first, then pick the border color below.

sections.title: Set button color
sections.summary: Hex color for button background. Default yellow-gold (#ffc201). Primary visual element for call-to-action buttons.

sections.title: Set button border color
sections.summary: Hex color for button border line. Only visible when border width is greater than 0.

sections.title: Set button border thickness
sections.summary: Button border stroke width in pixels (0-50). Default 0 (no border). Used with border color for outlined button style.

sections.title: Round button corners
sections.summary: Uniform corner radius (0-50 pixels) for all button corners. Default 12 creates slightly rounded button. Higher values create pill-shaped buttons.

sections.title: Button visual effects
sections.summary: Optional finishing touches for the button, such as overall transparency and entrance or tap animations. Use a subtle animation to draw the eye to a primary call-to-action, or lower the transparency to play down a secondary button. Leave it off for a plain, static button.

sections.title: Gradient color fill
sections.summary: Optional. Layers a color gradient over the button's solid background for a richer, more premium look. Pick Simple (two colors), Medium (two colors plus a tilt angle), or Advanced (several color stops, with optional shimmer). Leave it off if a flat color is enough; turn it on to make a primary button catch the eye.

sections.title: Optional icon on the button
sections.summary: Adds a small image beside the button label, positioned left or right of the text, with controls for its size and surrounding spacing. Use a simple icon to reinforce the action — like an arrow on a 'Continue' button — and upload a transparent PNG or SVG so it sits cleanly. Leave it empty for a clean text-only button.

sections.title: Inner spacing around the label
sections.summary: Sets the breathing room between the label or icon and the button's edges, set separately for top, bottom, left, and right. More padding makes the button bigger and easier to tap; too little makes it look cramped. Generous top and bottom padding gives a primary button a comfortable, finger-friendly tap area.

sections.title: Drop shadow under the button
sections.summary: Optional. Casts a soft shadow beneath the button so it appears lifted off the screen, which helps a primary action stand out. Adjust blur for softness, spread for size, opacity for strength, and offset for direction. A subtle shadow usually looks best; leave it off for a flat, minimal style.

sections.title: Align button text
sections.summary: Text alignment within button: start (left in LTR), center, or end (right in LTR). Center alignment is typical for buttons.

sections.title: Set button text color
sections.summary: Hex color for button label text. Default black (#000000). Must contrast with button background for readability.

sections.title: Font for the button text
sections.summary: Picks the typeface used for the button label. Leave it on your theme default so the button matches the rest of your funnel — mixing fonts on one screen looks unpolished and can hurt trust. Only override it when your brand requires a specific font.

sections.title: Size of the button label
sections.summary: Sets how large the text on the button appears. Most buttons read well at 16-18; go larger to make a primary action more prominent, but watch that the label doesn't wrap or overflow on small phone screens. Keep it consistent across your buttons so the screen looks intentional.

sections.title: Boldness of the label
sections.summary: Sets how thick the button text is, from 400 (regular) through 700 (bold) and beyond. Bolder text draws the eye, so use 600-700 for a primary action you want people to tap. Keep lighter weights for secondary or less important buttons.

sections.title: Spacing between wrapped lines
sections.summary: Sets the vertical gap between lines when a button label is long enough to wrap onto two or more lines. Most buttons use a single short label, so the default is fine and you can ignore this. Nudge it up only if a multi-line button looks cramped or hard to read.

sections.title: Wording on the button
sections.summary: The text shown on the button (placeholder 'Button Text'). Use a short, action-led phrase like 'Continue', 'Get Started', or 'Next' so people know exactly what tapping does. If your funnel runs in more than one language, this wording is saved per language, so set it for each one you support.

sections.title: Space around the whole section stack
sections.summary: Container padding adds space between the phone edges and all sections on the screen. It is different from Section padding: container padding moves the entire stack inward, while section padding adds space inside one selected section. Use container padding first when every block feels too close to the screen edge, then use per-section padding only where a specific block needs more breathing room.

sections.title: Round the section corners
sections.summary: Rounds all four corners of the section. The default 0 keeps them sharp and square; higher values (try 8 to 16) give a soft card look that pairs well with a solid background or border to make the section stand out as its own block. The range is 0 to 50 pixels.

sections.title: Delete a section
sections.summary: Use the trash icon to remove a section from the screen. Deleting also removes that section's content and can affect buttons linked to it, so confirm only after checking the preview and any parent-section links. If you are unsure, rename the section first or move it lower in the order while you verify the layout instead of deleting it immediately.

sections.title: Stretch to fill empty space
sections.summary: Controls how much leftover vertical space a section soaks up so the screen has no awkward gap. 0 keeps a section at its natural size (the default for text and buttons); 1 or more lets it stretch, and a section set to 2 takes twice the extra space as one set to 1. Raise this on your image or hero section to push the button down to a comfortable spot. Only applies when the section isn't set to scroll.

sections.title: Let it shrink on small screens
sections.summary: Controls which section gives up height first when everything can't fit on a small phone. Higher numbers shrink sooner; 0 means never shrink this one. The default of 1 lets sections shrink evenly. Set 0 on must-stay pieces like the button or logo, and raise it on a less important section like a tall image, so the key content survives intact on the smallest screens.

sections.title: How tall this section is
sections.summary: Decides how the section's height is calculated. Auto (the safe default) makes it exactly as tall as its content, which is right for most text and buttons. Fixed lets you type an exact pixel height, and Percent sets it to a share of the screen, handy for a hero image that should always fill, say, the top 40 percent. Your pick also decides which value box below applies.

sections.title: The height number
sections.summary: This is the number that pairs with your height mode. With Fixed mode, type pixels (0 to 1000, for example 320 for a tall hero); with Percent mode, type a share of the screen (0 to 100, for example 40). The box is ignored in Auto mode. For a scrollable section, this also sets the visible window the content scrolls inside.

sections.title: Left, center, or right
sections.summary: Positions the content along the section's width: Left, Center, or Right. Center is the usual choice for headlines and buttons, while Left reads more naturally for longer body copy. (Left and right follow text direction, so they flip on right-to-left languages.)

sections.title: Link the Purchase Button to the same catalog
sections.summary: Use the Purchase Button’s “Linked to section” dropdown to select the same Product Catalog section. This keeps the CTA tied to the visitor’s selected plan instead of a fixed product.

sections.title: Link product-aware sections
sections.summary: Some Flexible Layout sections can read the visitor’s current Product Catalog selection. For a paywall, add a Product Catalog section, then link a Text section and a Purchase Button section to that catalog through each section’s “Linked to section” dropdown. The linked Text section can show the selected product description label, and the linked Purchase Button can show the selected product purchase label.

sections.title: Space between sections
sections.summary: Margin is the gap outside a section, between it and the sections next to it. Set Top, Bottom, Left, and Right independently, using positive values to push sections apart. A negative top margin pulls a section up so it overlaps the one above — for example, a headline resting on a hero image; pair that with stacking order to control what sits in front.

sections.title: Text below or over the image
sections.summary: Decides whether your text and buttons sit below the image or float on top of it. Below media keeps content in its own space under the image — the safest choice for readability. Overlapping media lets the headline drift over the lower part of the image for a magazine-style hero; if you use it, add an overlay or gradient so the text stays legible against the picture.

sections.title: Round the image corners
sections.summary: Rounds the corners of the image or video. The default 0 is square; try 8 to 16 for a soft, modern look or a higher value for a strongly rounded card. Match it to the rounding on nearby buttons and sections so the whole screen feels cohesive.

sections.title: Dark fade for readable text
sections.summary: Adds a dark fade over the bottom of the image or video so text placed on top stays readable. It's strongest at the bottom and clears toward the top. The default is black, which is the usual choice (or a dark brand color). Use it whenever you let content overlap the media so your headline and button don't get lost in a busy image.

sections.title: How much height the image takes
sections.summary: Sets how much of the section's height the image or video fills, as a percentage. The default 50 splits the space evenly and leaves the lower half for your headline and button. Raise it (around 70) for a bold, image-led screen, or lower it when you need more room for copy and a clear call to action.

sections.title: Loop the video
sections.summary: For video media only: turn on to loop the clip continuously, or leave off to play it once and stop. Looping suits short, ambient hero or background videos that keep the screen feeling alive, while play-once suits a clip with a clear start and finish. It has no effect on still images.

sections.title: How the image fills its area
sections.summary: Decides how your image or video fits the section. Fill covers the whole area and crops the edges that don't fit — best for full-bleed hero shots and the right pick for most ad creatives. Fit shows the entire image but may leave blank bars around it; use it when nothing can be cropped. Stretch forces an exact fit but distorts the picture, so avoid it for photos.

sections.title: Where the image starts on screen
sections.summary: Sets the top edge of your image or video. Screen Top runs it all the way up behind the status bar and header for a full-bleed, edge-to-edge hero. Header Bottom starts it just below the header bar so a back button or progress bar stays clearly visible. Pick Screen Top for an immersive opener, Header Bottom when the header needs to read cleanly.

sections.title: Open one section's settings
sections.summary: Click the gear inside a section card to open that section's own settings. The first panel controls the section container — height, flex, scrollability, background, borders, alignment, padding, and margin — and the panel below controls the section's content, such as text, media, products, or button styling. This is the main place to tune how one block looks and behaves.

sections.title: Breathing room inside the section
sections.summary: Padding is the space inside a section, between its edges and the content sitting in it. Set Top, Bottom, Left, and Right independently, starting from 0. Add some so text and buttons don't crowd the section border or a background image; 16-24 px all around is a comfortable, readable starting point.

sections.title: Set purchase button color
sections.summary: Hex color for purchase button background. Default yellow-gold (#ffc201). Distinguishes purchase action from regular navigation.

sections.title: Purchase button border color
sections.summary: Sets the color of the outline around the purchase button. It only shows up when the border thickness is above 0, so set a thickness first. Use it to give an outlined-style call-to-action a clean, contrasting edge.

sections.title: Purchase button border thickness
sections.summary: Sets how thick the outline around the purchase button is, from 0 to 50 pixels. The default is 0, meaning no border; set a value together with a border color to create an outlined button. A solid filled button usually converts better, so most paywalls leave this at 0.

sections.title: Roundness of the button corners
sections.summary: Rounds all four corners of the purchase button by the same amount, from sharp to fully rounded (0-50). The default of about 12 gives a softly rounded look; raise it toward 50 for a pill-shaped button, or set 0 for crisp square corners. Match it to your other buttons so the paywall feels cohesive.

sections.title: Offer a cheaper plan on cancel
sections.summary: Controls what happens when someone cancels the payment. When on, they're sent to a downsale screen offering a cheaper or alternative plan — a second chance to recover the sale. When off, cancelling just sends them back with no further offer. Only turn this on if you've actually built a downsale screen in the funnel, otherwise there's nothing for it to open.

sections.title: Purchase button effects
sections.summary: Optional finishing touches for the purchase button, such as overall transparency and entrance or tap animations. A subtle pulse or scale animation can pull attention to your call-to-action and lift conversions. Leave it off for a static button.

sections.title: Purchase button gradient
sections.summary: Optionally lays a color gradient over the button's solid background for a richer call-to-action. Pick Simple (two colors), Medium (two colors plus an angle), or Advanced (multiple color stops, with an optional shimmer). Use it to make your main CTA pop; leave it off if a flat color already stands out.

sections.title: Purchase button icon
sections.summary: Optionally shows a small image next to the button label, to the left or right of the text. Upload an icon, then set its size and the spacing around it. A lock or arrow icon can reinforce the action, but a clean text-only button works just as well.

sections.title: Inner spacing around the label
sections.summary: Sets the breathing room between the label or icon and the purchase button's edges, set separately for top, bottom, left, and right. More padding makes the button taller and easier to tap; too little looks cramped. Generous top and bottom padding helps your main purchase button feel substantial and inviting to press.

sections.title: Purchase button shadow
sections.summary: Optionally adds a soft shadow beneath the button so it lifts off the screen and pulls the eye toward your call-to-action. You can tune the softness (blur), size (spread), strength (opacity), and direction (offset). A subtle shadow usually works best; leave it off for a flat design.

sections.title: Purchase button text alignment
sections.summary: Sets where the label sits inside the button: start (left in left-to-right languages), center, or end (right). Center is the standard choice and is recommended for a call-to-action so the label reads as one clear, balanced action.

sections.title: Purchase button text color
sections.summary: Sets the color of the words on your purchase button. Make sure it contrasts strongly with the button background so the label stays easy to read — for example, dark text on the default yellow-gold button. Weak contrast means users miss the action, which directly costs you conversions.

sections.title: Purchase button font
sections.summary: Picks the typeface for the purchase button label, such as SF Pro or Helvetica. Match it to the rest of your paywall so the call-to-action looks intentional rather than out of place. Leave it on the theme default unless your brand uses a specific font.

sections.title: Purchase button text size
sections.summary: Sets how big the label on your purchase button looks, measured in points. Since this is your main paywall call-to-action, keep it large and unmistakable — around 17 to 20 pt works well on most screens. Avoid going so big that the text wraps or spills outside the button on smaller phones.

sections.title: Purchase button text weight
sections.summary: Controls how thick or bold the button label appears, on a scale from 400 (regular) to 700 (bold) and heavier. As your primary call-to-action it should look bold and confident — a weight of 600 to 700 helps it visually dominate any secondary buttons on the screen.

sections.title: Purchase button line spacing
sections.summary: Controls the vertical gap between lines when the button label runs onto two or more lines. Most call-to-action labels fit on one line, so you can leave this on the default. Adjust it only if a longer label looks cramped or too loose when it wraps.

sections.title: Wording on the buy button
sections.summary: The text on your paywall's purchase button (default 'Subscribe Now'). This is the most important call to action in the whole funnel, so make it clear and benefit-led, such as 'Start My Free Trial' or 'Unlock Full Access'. If you run multiple languages, this wording is saved per language, so translate it for each.

sections.title: Reorder sections
sections.summary: Drag the handle beside a section name to change the vertical reading order on the screen. The order here is the order visitors see in the preview and published flow, so keep the persuasion sequence clear: context first, offer/details next, then the CTA. After reordering, recheck fixed-height and flex settings because a section that worked in one position may need different spacing in another.

sections.title: Let the whole screen scroll
sections.summary: When Scrollable screen is on, sections stack vertically and the visitor can scroll through them. Use this for long paywalls, product catalogs, benefit lists, or any screen with more content than fits on a phone. When it is off, the screen uses flexGrow and flexShrink to distribute sections inside one viewport, which is better for fixed hero layouts where the CTA should stay visible without scrolling.

sections.title: Open screen-level layout settings
sections.summary: The gear beside the Sections title opens settings for the whole FlexibleLayout screen, not for one individual section. Use it to control whether the full screen scrolls and how much padding the whole stack has from the screen edges. Open this before editing individual section padding when the entire screen feels too close to the phone edge or when you need a fixed, non-scrolling composition.

sections.title: Let this section scroll on its own
sections.summary: Turn on to let a section scroll independently when its content is taller than the height you set (works only with a Fixed or Percent height, not Auto). Use it for a long list of terms or bullets you want capped inside a fixed window while the rest of the screen stays put. Leave off (the default) for normal sections that just sit in the layout.

sections.title: Rename a section for editing
sections.summary: Click the pencil beside a section name to give it a clear internal label, such as Hero headline, Annual plan list, or Bottom CTA. This name helps editors understand the structure and is not shown to visitors. Rename repeated sections immediately so it is obvious which block you are opening, especially when several Text or Button sections exist on the same screen.

sections.title: Selected product drives labels and purchase
sections.summary: When the visitor changes the selected plan, linked labels update from that selected product. If you leave the Text title empty, it falls back to the product’s description label. If you leave the Purchase Button label empty, it falls back to the product’s purchase label. When the button is linked to the catalog, tapping it purchases the selected product, not a fixed default product.

sections.title: Verify checkout uses the selected product
sections.summary: For paid-trial, no-trial, and one-time products, verify a payment_intent with non-empty amount and currency. For free-trial subscriptions, verify setup_intent. This proves the linked purchase button buys the currently selected product.

sections.title: Updated selected product labels
sections.summary: After selecting a different Product Catalog item, the linked Text label and Purchase Button label update to that product’s description and purchase labels.

sections.title: Left, center, or right text
sections.summary: Sets whether the text reads from the Left, Center, or Right. Center suits short headlines and call-to-action lines, while Left is easier to read for longer body copy. (Left and right follow language direction and flip on right-to-left locales.)

sections.title: Text color
sections.summary: Sets the color of this text. The default is black. Always check it against the section background: dark text on light backgrounds, and light or white text over dark or image backgrounds. Low-contrast text is hard to read and a common reason visitors bounce, so keep your message legible.

sections.title: Pick the font
sections.summary: Sets which typeface this text uses. By default it follows your theme font, which keeps the whole funnel looking consistent, so change it only for a deliberate accent. Stick to one or two fonts across the funnel so it reads as polished and on-brand to paid visitors.

sections.title: Text size
sections.summary: Sets the font size in points, where bigger means more prominent. As a guide, about 24 to 40 works for a headline and 14 to 18 for body copy, keeping a clear hierarchy. This overrides your theme's default size for this text, so change it only when this section needs to stand apart from the rest.

sections.title: How heavy the text looks
sections.summary: Controls how thick the text appears. Common picks are 400 for regular body copy, 600 for semibold, and 700 for bold headlines and call-to-action lines. Put the heaviest weight on the one line you most want visitors to notice and keep body text lighter, so the screen has an easy-to-read hierarchy.

sections.title: Spacing between lines
sections.summary: Controls the vertical gap between lines in a multi-line block. Roughly 1.3 to 1.5 times the font size reads comfortably for body copy, with tighter spacing for big headlines. Bump it up if a paragraph feels cramped, or down if a headline's lines drift apart. It only matters when text wraps to more than one line.

sections.title: The words in this section
sections.summary: Sets the headline or body text shown here. You can drop in dynamic values by typing @ to pick a flow variable, so the screen can echo the visitor's earlier answer, show a label, or run a live countdown, which makes the funnel feel personal and converts better. If your funnel runs in more than one language, this text can be translated per language.

sections.title: Top, center, or bottom
sections.summary: Pins the content to the Top, Center, or Bottom of the section. It only changes anything when the section is taller than its content, for example with a Fixed or Percent height or a section stretched to fill space. Use Center to vertically center a headline in a tall hero, or Bottom to push a caption to the base of an image.

sections.title: Which section sits in front
sections.summary: When two sections overlap, this decides which one shows on top. A higher number wins; the default 0 is fine as long as nothing overlaps. You only need it when you've deliberately layered sections, like a headline placed over a background image, so give the part you want visible the higher number.

subarticles.title: Background fill color
subarticles.summary: Sets the color behind this section's content, used when the background type is Solid. The default is white. Enter a hex code or pick a swatch, and keep it in line with your theme so the screen feels on-brand, with enough contrast against the text on top to stay readable.

subarticles.title: Solid color or image behind
subarticles.summary: Sets what fills the area behind this section's content. Solid (the default) uses one color you pick below; Media places an image behind the content for a richer, ad-style look. If you go with Media and put text on top, keep the text readable with a darker image or an overlay so your value proposition doesn't get lost.

subarticles.title: Outline color
subarticles.summary: Sets the color of the section's outline. The default is black, and it only shows when the border thickness is above 0, so set a width first. Match it to one of your theme's accent colors for a clean, on-brand frame around the section.

subarticles.title: Outline thickness
subarticles.summary: Draws an outline around the section. The default 0 means no border; 1 to 2 pixels gives a subtle frame that makes a section read as a self-contained card or highlights an offer. Set this above 0 first, then pick the border color below.

subarticles.title: Set button color
subarticles.summary: Hex color for button background. Default yellow-gold (#ffc201). Primary visual element for call-to-action buttons.

subarticles.title: Set button border color
subarticles.summary: Hex color for button border line. Only visible when border width is greater than 0.

subarticles.title: Set button border thickness
subarticles.summary: Button border stroke width in pixels (0-50). Default 0 (no border). Used with border color for outlined button style.

subarticles.title: Round button corners
subarticles.summary: Uniform corner radius (0-50 pixels) for all button corners. Default 12 creates slightly rounded button. Higher values create pill-shaped buttons.

subarticles.title: Button visual effects
subarticles.summary: Optional finishing touches for the button, such as overall transparency and entrance or tap animations. Use a subtle animation to draw the eye to a primary call-to-action, or lower the transparency to play down a secondary button. Leave it off for a plain, static button.

subarticles.title: Gradient color fill
subarticles.summary: Optional. Layers a color gradient over the button's solid background for a richer, more premium look. Pick Simple (two colors), Medium (two colors plus a tilt angle), or Advanced (several color stops, with optional shimmer). Leave it off if a flat color is enough; turn it on to make a primary button catch the eye.

subarticles.title: Optional icon on the button
subarticles.summary: Adds a small image beside the button label, positioned left or right of the text, with controls for its size and surrounding spacing. Use a simple icon to reinforce the action — like an arrow on a 'Continue' button — and upload a transparent PNG or SVG so it sits cleanly. Leave it empty for a clean text-only button.

subarticles.title: Inner spacing around the label
subarticles.summary: Sets the breathing room between the label or icon and the button's edges, set separately for top, bottom, left, and right. More padding makes the button bigger and easier to tap; too little makes it look cramped. Generous top and bottom padding gives a primary button a comfortable, finger-friendly tap area.

subarticles.title: Drop shadow under the button
subarticles.summary: Optional. Casts a soft shadow beneath the button so it appears lifted off the screen, which helps a primary action stand out. Adjust blur for softness, spread for size, opacity for strength, and offset for direction. A subtle shadow usually looks best; leave it off for a flat, minimal style.

subarticles.title: Align button text
subarticles.summary: Text alignment within button: start (left in LTR), center, or end (right in LTR). Center alignment is typical for buttons.

subarticles.title: Set button text color
subarticles.summary: Hex color for button label text. Default black (#000000). Must contrast with button background for readability.

subarticles.title: Font for the button text
subarticles.summary: Picks the typeface used for the button label. Leave it on your theme default so the button matches the rest of your funnel — mixing fonts on one screen looks unpolished and can hurt trust. Only override it when your brand requires a specific font.

subarticles.title: Size of the button label
subarticles.summary: Sets how large the text on the button appears. Most buttons read well at 16-18; go larger to make a primary action more prominent, but watch that the label doesn't wrap or overflow on small phone screens. Keep it consistent across your buttons so the screen looks intentional.

subarticles.title: Boldness of the label
subarticles.summary: Sets how thick the button text is, from 400 (regular) through 700 (bold) and beyond. Bolder text draws the eye, so use 600-700 for a primary action you want people to tap. Keep lighter weights for secondary or less important buttons.

subarticles.title: Spacing between wrapped lines
subarticles.summary: Sets the vertical gap between lines when a button label is long enough to wrap onto two or more lines. Most buttons use a single short label, so the default is fine and you can ignore this. Nudge it up only if a multi-line button looks cramped or hard to read.

subarticles.title: Wording on the button
subarticles.summary: The text shown on the button (placeholder 'Button Text'). Use a short, action-led phrase like 'Continue', 'Get Started', or 'Next' so people know exactly what tapping does. If your funnel runs in more than one language, this wording is saved per language, so set it for each one you support.

subarticles.title: Space around the whole section stack
subarticles.summary: Container padding adds space between the phone edges and all sections on the screen. It is different from Section padding: container padding moves the entire stack inward, while section padding adds space inside one selected section. Use container padding first when every block feels too close to the screen edge, then use per-section padding only where a specific block needs more breathing room.

subarticles.title: Round the section corners
subarticles.summary: Rounds all four corners of the section. The default 0 keeps them sharp and square; higher values (try 8 to 16) give a soft card look that pairs well with a solid background or border to make the section stand out as its own block. The range is 0 to 50 pixels.

subarticles.title: Delete a section
subarticles.summary: Use the trash icon to remove a section from the screen. Deleting also removes that section's content and can affect buttons linked to it, so confirm only after checking the preview and any parent-section links. If you are unsure, rename the section first or move it lower in the order while you verify the layout instead of deleting it immediately.

subarticles.title: Stretch to fill empty space
subarticles.summary: Controls how much leftover vertical space a section soaks up so the screen has no awkward gap. 0 keeps a section at its natural size (the default for text and buttons); 1 or more lets it stretch, and a section set to 2 takes twice the extra space as one set to 1. Raise this on your image or hero section to push the button down to a comfortable spot. Only applies when the section isn't set to scroll.

subarticles.title: Let it shrink on small screens
subarticles.summary: Controls which section gives up height first when everything can't fit on a small phone. Higher numbers shrink sooner; 0 means never shrink this one. The default of 1 lets sections shrink evenly. Set 0 on must-stay pieces like the button or logo, and raise it on a less important section like a tall image, so the key content survives intact on the smallest screens.

subarticles.title: How tall this section is
subarticles.summary: Decides how the section's height is calculated. Auto (the safe default) makes it exactly as tall as its content, which is right for most text and buttons. Fixed lets you type an exact pixel height, and Percent sets it to a share of the screen, handy for a hero image that should always fill, say, the top 40 percent. Your pick also decides which value box below applies.

subarticles.title: The height number
subarticles.summary: This is the number that pairs with your height mode. With Fixed mode, type pixels (0 to 1000, for example 320 for a tall hero); with Percent mode, type a share of the screen (0 to 100, for example 40). The box is ignored in Auto mode. For a scrollable section, this also sets the visible window the content scrolls inside.

subarticles.title: Left, center, or right
subarticles.summary: Positions the content along the section's width: Left, Center, or Right. Center is the usual choice for headlines and buttons, while Left reads more naturally for longer body copy. (Left and right follow text direction, so they flip on right-to-left languages.)

subarticles.title: Link the Purchase Button to the same catalog
subarticles.summary: Use the Purchase Button’s “Linked to section” dropdown to select the same Product Catalog section. This keeps the CTA tied to the visitor’s selected plan instead of a fixed product.

subarticles.title: Link product-aware sections
subarticles.summary: Some Flexible Layout sections can read the visitor’s current Product Catalog selection. For a paywall, add a Product Catalog section, then link a Text section and a Purchase Button section to that catalog through each section’s “Linked to section” dropdown. The linked Text section can show the selected product description label, and the linked Purchase Button can show the selected product purchase label.

subarticles.title: Space between sections
subarticles.summary: Margin is the gap outside a section, between it and the sections next to it. Set Top, Bottom, Left, and Right independently, using positive values to push sections apart. A negative top margin pulls a section up so it overlaps the one above — for example, a headline resting on a hero image; pair that with stacking order to control what sits in front.

subarticles.title: Text below or over the image
subarticles.summary: Decides whether your text and buttons sit below the image or float on top of it. Below media keeps content in its own space under the image — the safest choice for readability. Overlapping media lets the headline drift over the lower part of the image for a magazine-style hero; if you use it, add an overlay or gradient so the text stays legible against the picture.

subarticles.title: Round the image corners
subarticles.summary: Rounds the corners of the image or video. The default 0 is square; try 8 to 16 for a soft, modern look or a higher value for a strongly rounded card. Match it to the rounding on nearby buttons and sections so the whole screen feels cohesive.

subarticles.title: Dark fade for readable text
subarticles.summary: Adds a dark fade over the bottom of the image or video so text placed on top stays readable. It's strongest at the bottom and clears toward the top. The default is black, which is the usual choice (or a dark brand color). Use it whenever you let content overlap the media so your headline and button don't get lost in a busy image.

subarticles.title: How much height the image takes
subarticles.summary: Sets how much of the section's height the image or video fills, as a percentage. The default 50 splits the space evenly and leaves the lower half for your headline and button. Raise it (around 70) for a bold, image-led screen, or lower it when you need more room for copy and a clear call to action.

subarticles.title: Loop the video
subarticles.summary: For video media only: turn on to loop the clip continuously, or leave off to play it once and stop. Looping suits short, ambient hero or background videos that keep the screen feeling alive, while play-once suits a clip with a clear start and finish. It has no effect on still images.

subarticles.title: How the image fills its area
subarticles.summary: Decides how your image or video fits the section. Fill covers the whole area and crops the edges that don't fit — best for full-bleed hero shots and the right pick for most ad creatives. Fit shows the entire image but may leave blank bars around it; use it when nothing can be cropped. Stretch forces an exact fit but distorts the picture, so avoid it for photos.

subarticles.title: Where the image starts on screen
subarticles.summary: Sets the top edge of your image or video. Screen Top runs it all the way up behind the status bar and header for a full-bleed, edge-to-edge hero. Header Bottom starts it just below the header bar so a back button or progress bar stays clearly visible. Pick Screen Top for an immersive opener, Header Bottom when the header needs to read cleanly.

subarticles.title: Open one section's settings
subarticles.summary: Click the gear inside a section card to open that section's own settings. The first panel controls the section container — height, flex, scrollability, background, borders, alignment, padding, and margin — and the panel below controls the section's content, such as text, media, products, or button styling. This is the main place to tune how one block looks and behaves.

subarticles.title: Breathing room inside the section
subarticles.summary: Padding is the space inside a section, between its edges and the content sitting in it. Set Top, Bottom, Left, and Right independently, starting from 0. Add some so text and buttons don't crowd the section border or a background image; 16-24 px all around is a comfortable, readable starting point.

subarticles.title: Set purchase button color
subarticles.summary: Hex color for purchase button background. Default yellow-gold (#ffc201). Distinguishes purchase action from regular navigation.

subarticles.title: Purchase button border color
subarticles.summary: Sets the color of the outline around the purchase button. It only shows up when the border thickness is above 0, so set a thickness first. Use it to give an outlined-style call-to-action a clean, contrasting edge.

subarticles.title: Purchase button border thickness
subarticles.summary: Sets how thick the outline around the purchase button is, from 0 to 50 pixels. The default is 0, meaning no border; set a value together with a border color to create an outlined button. A solid filled button usually converts better, so most paywalls leave this at 0.

subarticles.title: Roundness of the button corners
subarticles.summary: Rounds all four corners of the purchase button by the same amount, from sharp to fully rounded (0-50). The default of about 12 gives a softly rounded look; raise it toward 50 for a pill-shaped button, or set 0 for crisp square corners. Match it to your other buttons so the paywall feels cohesive.

subarticles.title: Offer a cheaper plan on cancel
subarticles.summary: Controls what happens when someone cancels the payment. When on, they're sent to a downsale screen offering a cheaper or alternative plan — a second chance to recover the sale. When off, cancelling just sends them back with no further offer. Only turn this on if you've actually built a downsale screen in the funnel, otherwise there's nothing for it to open.

subarticles.title: Purchase button effects
subarticles.summary: Optional finishing touches for the purchase button, such as overall transparency and entrance or tap animations. A subtle pulse or scale animation can pull attention to your call-to-action and lift conversions. Leave it off for a static button.

subarticles.title: Purchase button gradient
subarticles.summary: Optionally lays a color gradient over the button's solid background for a richer call-to-action. Pick Simple (two colors), Medium (two colors plus an angle), or Advanced (multiple color stops, with an optional shimmer). Use it to make your main CTA pop; leave it off if a flat color already stands out.

subarticles.title: Purchase button icon
subarticles.summary: Optionally shows a small image next to the button label, to the left or right of the text. Upload an icon, then set its size and the spacing around it. A lock or arrow icon can reinforce the action, but a clean text-only button works just as well.

subarticles.title: Inner spacing around the label
subarticles.summary: Sets the breathing room between the label or icon and the purchase button's edges, set separately for top, bottom, left, and right. More padding makes the button taller and easier to tap; too little looks cramped. Generous top and bottom padding helps your main purchase button feel substantial and inviting to press.

subarticles.title: Purchase button shadow
subarticles.summary: Optionally adds a soft shadow beneath the button so it lifts off the screen and pulls the eye toward your call-to-action. You can tune the softness (blur), size (spread), strength (opacity), and direction (offset). A subtle shadow usually works best; leave it off for a flat design.

subarticles.title: Purchase button text alignment
subarticles.summary: Sets where the label sits inside the button: start (left in left-to-right languages), center, or end (right). Center is the standard choice and is recommended for a call-to-action so the label reads as one clear, balanced action.

subarticles.title: Purchase button text color
subarticles.summary: Sets the color of the words on your purchase button. Make sure it contrasts strongly with the button background so the label stays easy to read — for example, dark text on the default yellow-gold button. Weak contrast means users miss the action, which directly costs you conversions.

subarticles.title: Purchase button font
subarticles.summary: Picks the typeface for the purchase button label, such as SF Pro or Helvetica. Match it to the rest of your paywall so the call-to-action looks intentional rather than out of place. Leave it on the theme default unless your brand uses a specific font.

subarticles.title: Purchase button text size
subarticles.summary: Sets how big the label on your purchase button looks, measured in points. Since this is your main paywall call-to-action, keep it large and unmistakable — around 17 to 20 pt works well on most screens. Avoid going so big that the text wraps or spills outside the button on smaller phones.

subarticles.title: Purchase button text weight
subarticles.summary: Controls how thick or bold the button label appears, on a scale from 400 (regular) to 700 (bold) and heavier. As your primary call-to-action it should look bold and confident — a weight of 600 to 700 helps it visually dominate any secondary buttons on the screen.

subarticles.title: Purchase button line spacing
subarticles.summary: Controls the vertical gap between lines when the button label runs onto two or more lines. Most call-to-action labels fit on one line, so you can leave this on the default. Adjust it only if a longer label looks cramped or too loose when it wraps.

subarticles.title: Wording on the buy button
subarticles.summary: The text on your paywall's purchase button (default 'Subscribe Now'). This is the most important call to action in the whole funnel, so make it clear and benefit-led, such as 'Start My Free Trial' or 'Unlock Full Access'. If you run multiple languages, this wording is saved per language, so translate it for each.

subarticles.title: Reorder sections
subarticles.summary: Drag the handle beside a section name to change the vertical reading order on the screen. The order here is the order visitors see in the preview and published flow, so keep the persuasion sequence clear: context first, offer/details next, then the CTA. After reordering, recheck fixed-height and flex settings because a section that worked in one position may need different spacing in another.

subarticles.title: Let the whole screen scroll
subarticles.summary: When Scrollable screen is on, sections stack vertically and the visitor can scroll through them. Use this for long paywalls, product catalogs, benefit lists, or any screen with more content than fits on a phone. When it is off, the screen uses flexGrow and flexShrink to distribute sections inside one viewport, which is better for fixed hero layouts where the CTA should stay visible without scrolling.

subarticles.title: Open screen-level layout settings
subarticles.summary: The gear beside the Sections title opens settings for the whole FlexibleLayout screen, not for one individual section. Use it to control whether the full screen scrolls and how much padding the whole stack has from the screen edges. Open this before editing individual section padding when the entire screen feels too close to the phone edge or when you need a fixed, non-scrolling composition.

subarticles.title: Let this section scroll on its own
subarticles.summary: Turn on to let a section scroll independently when its content is taller than the height you set (works only with a Fixed or Percent height, not Auto). Use it for a long list of terms or bullets you want capped inside a fixed window while the rest of the screen stays put. Leave off (the default) for normal sections that just sit in the layout.

subarticles.summary: Click the pencil beside a section name to give it a clear internal label, such as Hero headline, Annual plan list, or Bottom CTA. This name helps editors understand the structure and is not shown to visitors. Rename repeated sections immediately so it is obvious which block you are opening, especially when several Text or Button sections exist on the same screen.

subarticles.title: Selected product drives labels and purchase
subarticles.summary: When the visitor changes the selected plan, linked labels update from that selected product. If you leave the Text title empty, it falls back to the product’s description label. If you leave the Purchase Button label empty, it falls back to the product’s purchase label. When the button is linked to the catalog, tapping it purchases the selected product, not a fixed default product.

subarticles.title: Verify checkout uses the selected product
subarticles.summary: For paid-trial, no-trial, and one-time products, verify a payment_intent with non-empty amount and currency. For free-trial subscriptions, verify setup_intent. This proves the linked purchase button buys the currently selected product.

subarticles.title: Updated selected product labels
subarticles.summary: After selecting a different Product Catalog item, the linked Text label and Purchase Button label update to that product’s description and purchase labels.

subarticles.title: Left, center, or right text
subarticles.summary: Sets whether the text reads from the Left, Center, or Right. Center suits short headlines and call-to-action lines, while Left is easier to read for longer body copy. (Left and right follow language direction and flip on right-to-left locales.)

subarticles.title: Text color
subarticles.summary: Sets the color of this text. The default is black. Always check it against the section background: dark text on light backgrounds, and light or white text over dark or image backgrounds. Low-contrast text is hard to read and a common reason visitors bounce, so keep your message legible.

subarticles.title: Pick the font
subarticles.summary: Sets which typeface this text uses. By default it follows your theme font, which keeps the whole funnel looking consistent, so change it only for a deliberate accent. Stick to one or two fonts across the funnel so it reads as polished and on-brand to paid visitors.

subarticles.title: Text size
subarticles.summary: Sets the font size in points, where bigger means more prominent. As a guide, about 24 to 40 works for a headline and 14 to 18 for body copy, keeping a clear hierarchy. This overrides your theme's default size for this text, so change it only when this section needs to stand apart from the rest.

subarticles.title: How heavy the text looks
subarticles.summary: Controls how thick the text appears. Common picks are 400 for regular body copy, 600 for semibold, and 700 for bold headlines and call-to-action lines. Put the heaviest weight on the one line you most want visitors to notice and keep body text lighter, so the screen has an easy-to-read hierarchy.

subarticles.title: Spacing between lines
subarticles.summary: Controls the vertical gap between lines in a multi-line block. Roughly 1.3 to 1.5 times the font size reads comfortably for body copy, with tighter spacing for big headlines. Bump it up if a paragraph feels cramped, or down if a headline's lines drift apart. It only matters when text wraps to more than one line.

translations.en: Flexible Sections — every setting

The build-your-own screen — you stack sections (text, media, product catalog, buttons, lists…) and arrange them: add / reorder / rename / delete, set each section’s size, fill, alignment, border, padding and margin, control whole-screen scroll and padding, and link product-aware sections (for example Text or Purchase Button) to a Product Catalog so labels and purchases follow the selected product. Each section type’s own content and styling lives in its dedicated block article. This guide documents every setting of the Flexible Sections block, grouped by area. Each setting matches a real control in the screen editor.
